verdict.rationale: The evidence pack documents general Python/TypeScript SDKs, an MCP server, and a Claude Code plugin, but no integration with LiveKit, Pipecat, ElevenLabs or any other real-time voice pipeline. The claim that context() is 'efficient enough to use at every turn' is a general latency statement, not a documented voice integration. Generic SDKs are only building blocks a developer could use to construct such an integration, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can wire memory into real-time voice pipelines (e.g. LiveKit, Pipecat, ElevenLabs) with documented integrations fast enough for live conversation
